title: The Muscle Ladder – Program Selector
source: Jeff Nippard – The Muscle Ladder: Get Jacked Using Science (Chapter 15)
description: 4 required questions + 1 optional question. Each answer filters the 20 programs from Chapter 15 down to the one best suited to you. Q5 (split preference) is optional — it only comes into play when your first 4 answers result in a tie between 2 programs.

questions.question: What is your main goal?
questions.note: The book frames all 20 programs around muscle and strength gain. The goal question determines whether you follow the fully optimised version (more volume, more time) or the time-efficient version (leaner, faster). Fat loss and recomposition are achieved through diet, not a different program — the training stays the same.

options.label: Build muscle and gain strength (maximise results)
Build muscle and gain strength (limited time available)
Lose fat while maintaining muscle
options.diet_note: Training program is identical to muscle-building. Fat loss is driven by a 10–20% caloric deficit in your diet, not a different program. Pick the program that matches your level and schedule, then adjust your nutrition.

options.label: Body recomposition (lose fat and gain muscle simultaneously)
options.diet_note: Recomp is realistic especially for beginners and those with higher body fat. Keep calories at maintenance and prioritise protein. Same training program as muscle-building.

questions.question: What is your training experience level?
questions.note: Based on years of serious, consistent training — not just time spent in a gym casually.

options.label: Beginner
options.description: Under ~1 year of serious training. You make strength progress workout to workout. Beginner programs use more machine-based exercises, which are easier to learn safely.

options.label: Intermediate
options.description: 2–5 years of serious training. Progress happens week to week.

options.label: Advanced
options.description: 5–10 years of serious training. Progress happens over months. Requires higher volume and more training days to keep progressing.

questions.question: How many days per week can you consistently train?
questions.note: Sustainability is a core principle. A lower frequency you can stick to is always better than a higher frequency you can't. More days is not automatically better — recovery matters equally.

questions.question: What equipment do you have access to?
questions.note: The book states that exercise selection matters less than technique, effort, and volume. Every exercise in every program has 2 substitution options for missing equipment. Equipment primarily affects which exercises you do within a program — not which program number you follow. However, a full commercial gym unlocks all programs equally, while limited setups may constrain some splits.

options.label: Full commercial gym (barbells, dumbbells, cables, machines)
Home gym with barbell, dumbbells, rack and bench
options.constraint: minor — cable and machine exercises need substitution with free-weight equivalents. All splits still work.
options.substitution_note: Swap any cable or machine exercise for the free-weight alternative listed in each program. The book explicitly supports this.

options.label: Dumbbells only (home or limited gym)
options.constraint: moderate — barbell primary lifts (squat, bench, deadlift, OHP) need dumbbell substitutions. Full-body splits work best. Heavy compound progressions are harder to track.
options.substitution_note: Replace barbell exercises with dumbbell equivalents: DB goblet squat, DB Romanian deadlift, DB bench press, DB shoulder press. The book provides substitution options for every exercise.

options.label: Bodyweight only
options.constraint: significant — the book is designed around resistance training with weights. Bodyweight works for beginners at low frequencies but limits progression at intermediate/advanced levels.
options.substitution_note: The book's minimal example (3 exercises: goblet squat, push-up, dumbbell row) shows bodyweight can work at beginner level. Advanced progressions will be limited without added resistance.

questions.question: Do you have a preferred training split structure?
questions.note: This question only matters when your other answers return 2 programs (a tie). If you have no preference, skip it — both options in a tie are equally effective. Not all splits are available at every level and day combination; only the splits available to you based on Q1–Q4 will apply.

options.label: Full Body
options.description: Every session trains all major muscle groups. High frequency per muscle. Best for beginners and those who want flexibility — missing a session doesn't leave a muscle group untrained for the week.

options.label: Upper / Lower
options.description: Alternates between upper body days and lower body days. A clean, popular split for intermediate lifters. 4–6 days/week. Allows higher volume per session for each half of the body.

options.label: Push / Pull / Legs (PPL)
options.description: Push day (chest, shoulders, triceps), Pull day (back, biceps), Legs day — repeated twice over 6 days. Focused sessions, clear muscle group separation. A favourite for intermediate and advanced lifters at 6 days.

options.label: Hybrid (Upper/Lower + PPL)
options.description: Combines Upper/Lower and PPL across 5 days. More variety than either split alone. Best for intermediate and advanced lifters who want structured variety without going to 6 days.

options.label: No preference — let the other answers decide
options.description: Skip this question. The decision map will recommend both tied programs and you can choose freely.

how_it_resolves_ties.description: When Q1–Q4 return 2 programs, Q5 picks one. Map of ties and how Q5 resolves them:

ties.scenario: Beginner + 4 days + 60–90 min + Full gym or Home gym
Intermediate or Advanced + 4 days + 60–90 min + Full gym or Home gym
Any level + 4 days + 45–60 min + Full gym, Home gym, or Dumbbells
Intermediate or Advanced + 6 days + 60–90 min + Full gym
Any level + 6 days + 45–60 min + Full gym

programs.name: Full-Body Split 2x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Best starting point for beginners who can only commit to 2 days. Machine-based exercises recommended but free-weight swaps are fine.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 2x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym, home gym, or dumbbells only
programs.notes: Works for all levels when time per session is constrained. Fewer exercises, some supersets to maintain volume within the shorter window.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 3x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Ideal entry point for most beginners. 3 full-body sessions with rest days in between for full recovery.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 3x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Higher volume and more exercise variety than Program 3. Intermediate and advanced lifters need more total sets to keep progressing.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 3x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym, home gym, or dumbbells only
programs.notes: Streamlined version of 3x/week full body. Works across all levels when session time is tight.

programs.name: Upper/Lower Split 4x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Introduces the Upper/Lower split to beginners at 4 days. Allows dedicated focus on upper or lower body each session while still recovering well.

programs.name: Upper/Lower Split 4x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: One of the most popular and well-supported intermediate programs. Higher volume, more exercise variety, and greater intensity than the beginner version.

programs.name: Upper/Lower Split 4x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Time-efficient Upper/Lower. Supersets are used to fit quality volume into shorter sessions.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 4x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Alternative to Program 6 for beginners who prefer full-body training at 4 days rather than an Upper/Lower split.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 4x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym or home gym with barbell + dumbbells
programs.notes: Alternative to Program 7. Choose this over 7 if you prefer hitting each muscle group every session rather than splitting upper/lower.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 4x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym, home gym, or dumbbells only
programs.notes: Time-efficient full-body at 4 days. Alternative to Program 8 if you prefer full-body over Upper/Lower.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 5x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: High-frequency full-body for advanced lifters only. Demands strong recovery capacity. Not recommended for beginners or intermediates.

programs.name: Full-Body Split 5x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Advanced 5-day full-body condensed into shorter sessions. Best for advanced lifters with limited time but high training frequency.

programs.name: Upper/Lower + Push/Pull/Legs Hybrid 5x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Combines the Upper/Lower and PPL structures across 5 days. More variety and greater per-muscle frequency than a standard 5-day split.

programs.name: Upper/Lower + Push/Pull/Legs Hybrid 5x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Time-efficient hybrid 5-day. The 'all levels' label means the time constraint is the dominant factor here, not experience.

programs.name: Upper/Lower Split 6x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Very high volume Upper/Lower. 3 upper days and 3 lower days per week. Requires solid recovery habits: sleep, nutrition, and stress management.

programs.name: Upper/Lower Split 6x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: High frequency but shorter sessions. Useful when you can train 6 days but have limited time each day.

programs.name: Push/Pull/Legs Split 6x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Beginner PPL at 6 days. Each muscle group is hit twice per week. Sessions are focused and shorter per body part compared to full-body workouts.

programs.name: Push/Pull/Legs Split 6x/Week
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: Classic PPL for serious lifters. Higher volume and intensity than the beginner version. Each push, pull, and leg day is trained twice per week.

programs.name: Push/Pull/Legs Split 6x/Week (Time-Efficient)
programs.equipment_needed: Full gym
programs.notes: PPL at 6 days but each session kept to 45–60 min. Good when you love high frequency but are crunched for time per session.

decision_map.description: Combine your 4 answers to find your program. Key: goal → session duration (Q1), level → Q2, days → Q3, equipment → Q4 (secondary filter).

how_goal_maps_to_duration.Q1C_Lose_fat: 60–90 min programs (same training as muscle-building; fat loss via diet)
how_goal_maps_to_duration.Q1D_Recomposition: 60–90 min programs (same training as muscle-building; recomp via diet)

entries.equipment_note: Use dumbbell substitutions within Program 3 if no barbell.
Use dumbbell substitutions within Program 4 if no barbell.
Use dumbbell substitutions within Program 4 if no barbell.

entries.tiebreaker: Program 6 = Upper/Lower. Program 9 = Full Body. Same muscle stimulus, different structure. Pick whichever split you prefer.

entries.equipment_note: Full Body is better suited to dumbbell-only setups. Use dumbbell substitutions within Program 9.

entries.tiebreaker: Program 7 = Upper/Lower. Program 10 = Full Body. Upper/Lower is slightly more common at this level, but both are equally effective.
Program 7 = Upper/Lower. Program 10 = Full Body. Same tiebreaker as intermediate.
Program 8 = Upper/Lower time-efficient. Program 11 = Full Body time-efficient. Pick based on split preference.
Program 12 = Full Body 5x (advanced only, very high frequency). Program 14 = Hybrid Upper/Lower + PPL (more split variety). Program 14 is more commonly recommended.
Program 13 = Full Body 5x time-efficient (advanced only). Program 15 = Hybrid time-efficient (all levels). Program 13 is full-body frequency; Program 15 adds split structure.
Program 16 = Upper/Lower 6x (more volume per muscle per session). Program 19 = PPL 6x (more focused, shorter sessions per muscle group). Both train each muscle twice per week.
Same as intermediate. Program 16 = Upper/Lower. Program 19 = PPL.
Program 17 = Upper/Lower time-efficient. Program 20 = PPL time-efficient. Pick based on split preference.

equipment_substitution_guide.description: When you lack certain equipment, apply these swaps within whichever program is recommended. Every exercise in the book comes with 2 built-in substitution options.

rules.substitute_with: Dumbbell equivalent (e.g. cable fly → dumbbell fly, cable row → dumbbell row, cable curl → dumbbell curl)
Dumbbell equivalent (e.g. barbell squat → goblet squat, barbell bench press → DB bench press, barbell deadlift → DB Romanian deadlift, barbell OHP → DB shoulder press)
Free-weight compound equivalent (e.g. leg press → goblet squat, chest press machine → push-up or DB bench press)
DB row or cable row for vertical pull movements
